messages:
ana: Heads up — on canary-5 we're seeing steady process memory growth for streaming-chat sessions that run very long (tool loops). RSS creeps ~1.5–2GB over 8–12h per worker. Repro attached below.

raj: Oof. Is that resident or virtual? Any OOMs?

ana: Resident (RSS). No OOMs yet, just slow steady growth. CPU looks fine. No obvious leak in app logs.

morgan: Can you paste the pmap / smaps snapshot for a long-lived worker? Also which allocator (jemalloc/tcmalloc/system)?

ana: Allocator is jemalloc in our runtime. Here's a short smaps diff I took 6h apart (abbreviated):

```
# t=0 RSS=2.4G
Anonymous: 1.6G
MAPPED: 600M
# t=6h RSS=3.8G
Anonymous: 2.9G (+1.3G)
MAPPED: 750M
```

ana: Most growth in anonymous heap regions.

raj: That screams KV cache residency / fragmentation to me. Long contexts append lots of variable-length KV entries; we might be hitting slab fragmentation or retired pages waiting for a full reuse window. Any evidence of many small allocations?

morgan: Run jeprof / jemalloc stats or mallctl to get retained size / extent fragmentation. Try: `je-heapstats -p $PID` and `je-mallctl stats.arenas` if we have the tools on the image.

ana: Ran jemalloc reachability sampling. Abbrev output: `active: 3.8G, allocated: 2.2G, metadata: 120M, extents_retained: 1.4G` — extents_retained is high.

li: extents_retained being large sounds like pages not being returned to the OS. Could be due to our KV slab arena using hugepages or disabling MADV_DONTNEED. Any madvise calls?

ana: We don't explicitly madvise on eviction. The KV cache does free() entries but they go to jemalloc; jemalloc seems to keep extents.

dave: Two hypotheses: 1) fragmentation from many different sized KV entries (small vs large) -> allocator keeps many small extents; 2) KV eviction policy not triggering compaction/reuse quickly (reuse window too long), so entries get freed but not reallocated in-place.

raj: Can you trigger a synthetic workload that repeatedly writes/deletes keys with the same shapes as tool-loop chat? That will help differentiate allocator fragmentation vs true leak.

ana: Did that. Synthetic loop: create many short keys and evict them via simulated tool call every 10s. After 24h RSS still grew ~1.2G. Heap profiles show retained extents still increasing.

morgan: Try forcing jemalloc purging: `mallctl('arenas.purge')` or set `opt.purge` to aggressive in a canary. If RSS drops after purge, it's retention not true kernel leak.

ana: Ran arenas.purge on a live process — RSS dropped ~600MB immediately, but then resumed growth with same slope.

li: OK that implies churn + retained extents, not kernel-level leak. Could be fragmentation of extents such that purge only helps temporarily. We should test compacting KV storage: coalesce small entries into bigger contiguous allocations or reuse an arena specific to KV with different decay time.

dave: Also consider calling MADV_FREE (or MADV_DONTNEED) on large KV buffers when evicting; jemalloc will still own the pages but can release to OS if you madvise. We need to ensure data is zeroed or we are okay with lazy reclaim.

raj: Another angle: our kernel selection path sometimes switches execution kernels that allocate scratch buffers per request. If long sessions keep those scratch buffers alive in TLS or in gcache, they might be pinned. Any pinned pointers?

ana: I grepped code. The streaming path keeps a per-session KVRef vector for tool loop retries, we retain last N revisions (N=5) for fast rollback. For long loops N grows when retries happen because we append and fail to drop tombstones in some error paths.

morgan: Aha — that could cause logical retention (we think we freed entries but still hold references). Can you instrument KVRef.count/refcounts?

ana: Added quick logging: found ~0.5–1M small KVRef objects held per session after many tool retries. Many were stale due to an exception path that didn't call retire_kv_entry().

dave: That explains the portion that doesn't respond to jemalloc purge. Those are live objects, not freed. Which explains why purge dropped some RSS (the retained extents) but the long tail is still live.

raj: Great find. Fix the exception path to call retire_kv_entry() and run a long canary. Also add a health metric: kv_live_refs_per_session.

ana: Pushed a small fix to ensure retire_kv_entry() in both success and all error branches. Can we roll to canary-6?

infra-bot: deploy requested: canary-6 -> infra/canary-5. Approver: dave.

dave: Approved. Roll it.

ana: Rolled canary-6 ~1h ago. Early numbers: RSS slope reduced by ~70% on the same synthetic workload. Still some residual growth but much slower.

morgan: Good. We should still address allocator retention: consider a dedicated jemalloc arena for KV that has a faster decay / aggressive purge so freed pages return to OS more readily.

li: Agreed. Also add a periodic background compacter that coalesces small freed slabs every X minutes (configurable). Watch CPU impact.

raj: Action items:
- ana: monitor canary-6 for 48h and upload smaps diffs (assigned)
- morgan: prototype jemalloc arena with aggressive decay and a config flag (P1)
- dave: add kv_live_refs_per_session metric and alert if > threshold (P1)
- li: prototype compacter + madvise flow (P2)

ana: I'll attach current logs & short heap profile here: https://s3.redwood-internal/canary6/heap-profile-1784001.svg (flamegraph).

raj: Nice. If canary holds we can backport the retire_kv_entry() fix to prod. Also open a postmortem-style doc summarizing root cause (logical retention + allocator retention) and mitigations.

dave: One more note: add a test in integ that simulates tool-loop exceptions to prevent regression.

ana: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: action items logged in JIRA: RINF-4127, RINF-4128, RINF-4129.
